Recent work

95 New York agent websites, audited

A brokerage-heavy market hides a lot of quiet problems. Across two audit rounds I checked 95 agent websites and profiles across New York and documented 358 issues — 208 in the first round of 45 sites, then 150 more in a second round of 50. Here's what actually came up.

Issues found most often — round two

Share of the 50 sites checked in the second audit round:

Photos with no alt text39 / 50 sites
Generic page title, no keywords34 / 50 sites
No testimonials at all29 / 50 sites
30 of 45first-round sites were brokerage-platform profiles (Compass, Elliman, Corcoran)
15 of 45first-round sites were the agent's own or team websites

Real findings — and the fix offered with each one

Found on a profile

A $12.7M listing with a price typo

The price was typed as “$12,700,00”. → Fix: correct the figure and re-check every active listing for the same slip.

Found on a profile

Same apartment listed twice, two prices

One home at 88 Central Park West appeared twice at different prices. → Fix: remove the duplicate and keep one accurate listing.

Found on a profile

15 of 16 photos invisible to Google

Almost every photo had no alt text, so search engines couldn't read them. → Fix: write descriptive alt text for each image.

Found on a profile

Active Listings and Sold History — both empty

A working agent shown with nothing to sell and nothing sold. → Fix: populate both sections from current and past deals.

Found on a profile

Testimonials from the wrong brokerage

Reviews still named a previous brokerage the agent had left. → Fix: update the testimonials to the current brokerage and clients.

Found on a profile

No bio at all

No About section, no story, nothing for a seller to trust. → Fix: add a short, specific bio with areas served and recent results.

Findings are shown without agent names — the full named list goes to the agent it belongs to. Every finding above is real, from the November 2026 audits.

The method

How I check a website

Everything is checked from the outside — exactly what your clients and Google see. Nothing on your site is changed during a check.

1

Open the site

Does it load? What does a first-time visitor actually see?

2

Check the title

The browser tab title — generic template titles like just “Compass” or “Home” are an issue.

3

Check the description

The meta description in the page source — missing or duplicated descriptions cost clicks.

4

Check the main heading

Is there a proper H1, and does it say more than just a name?

5

Check every photo

Alt text present or empty? Empty alt text means Google can't understand the image.

6

Look for what's broken

Photos that don't load, links that go nowhere, sections left empty.

7

Read the content

Bio present? Testimonials real and current? Typos, old dates, repeated sections — all noted.

8

Write it up, with fixes

You get each issue in plain words, next to exactly how to solve it.

About

About Noman Tariq

I'm Noman Tariq, and I run NamesNests. I work with real estate agents in New York who are good at selling homes but hard to find on Google — usually not because their site is bad, but because it's unfinished: a template title here, photos Google can't read there, an empty listings section nobody noticed.

My work starts with research. I built a working sheet of 500 New York agents — their brokerages, websites, profiles and contact details — then audited sites from it one by one. The first round of 45 audits turned up 208 issues; a second round of 50 sites added 150 more. And this wasn't research that sat in a folder: 49 agents received their own findings personally by email, each one with the fixes for their site.

Alongside audits and fixes, I also offer website development: if you have no website of your own — or your current one needs rebuilding — I build it complete and SEO-ready from the start, with your listings, bio, testimonials and lead forms in place.

That's the approach I bring to every client: check first, show you exactly what's wrong, then fix it. No long reports you can't use — a clear list, in plain words, with the work done.
